summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of the University of Kansas (KU), covering its athletics (the Kansas Jayhawks, with 13 national championships and a famous men's basketball program), notable alumni, academic rankings, enrollment and tuition, and its campuses and schools. It also summarizes the school's founding history, from the 1863 state law creating the university in Lawrence to its opening in 1866.
one_line: Overview of the University of Kansas, covering its campuses, rankings, enrollment, tuition, Jayhawks athletics, notable alumni, and founding history.
key_facts: The University of Kansas (KU) is a public research university and the largest in the U.S. state of Kansas.
KU branch campuses are located in Lawrence, Wichita, Overland Park, Salina, and Kansas City, Kansas, with the main campus on Mount Oread in Lawrence.
The university was founded March 21, 1865 and opened in 1866.
On February 20, 1863, Kansas Governor Thomas Carney signed a bill creating the state university in Lawrence, conditioned on a $15,000 endowment and at least forty acres of land.
KU's sports teams, called the Kansas Jayhawks, compete in NCAA Division I and the Big 12 Conference.
KU has won thirteen National Championships, including five in men's basketball.
The KU women's track and field team won the NCAA outdoor title in Eugene, Oregon on June 8, 2013, the first University of Kansas women's team to win a national title.
The KU men's basketball team has won three NCAA tournament championships, in 1952, 1988, and 2008.
Enrollment at the Lawrence and Edwards campuses was 23,597 students in fall 2014, plus 3,371 at KU Medical Center, for a total of 26,968.
For 2014–15, in-state freshman tuition was $318 per credit hour and out-of-state freshman tuition was $828 per credit hour.
The Edwards Campus in Overland Park, established in 1993, had about 2,100 students with an average age of 32.
According to DesignIntelligence, the School of Architecture and Urban Design was named the best in the Midwest and ranked 11th among U.S. undergraduate architecture programs in 2012.
The School of Engineering was officially founded in 1891, although engineering degrees were awarded as early as 1873.
The University of Kansas Medical Center features the School of Medicine, School of Nursing, and School of Health Professions, with 3,349 students enrolled as of Fall 2013.
